newsitem.title: UK: Rail Regulator to start Railtrack review.
newsitem.headline: Rail Regulator to start Railtrack review.

text.p: Britain's rail industry regulator, voicing concern about Railtrack Plc's profits, said on Thursday it would begin immediately its review of the privatised rail infrastructure operator's contractual performance.

"There is still a very long way for Railtrack to deliver on its investment obligations, and thus secure the longer-term health of the network," said John Swift, head of regulator Ofrail, in a statement.
Railtrack's operating profits surged 15 percent to 339 million pounds ($553.2 million) in its first year since privatisation, beating analysts' estimates of 298-308 million pounds.
Railtrack's shares rose 7.5 pence to 653 by 1115 GMT.
Swift said he was concerned that the improvement in day-to-day performance may be costing funders of railway services too much.

He added that Railtrack's results showed it was 87 million pounds ahead of the position assumed at the time certain supplements to cover the cost to Railtrack of operating performance incentives was agreed.

"I will therefore want to establish whether the arrangements are offering value for money for funders and train operators and to be satisfied that the money allowed for in access charges is not providing disproportionate benefits to shareholders," Swift said, adding that he was bringing forward his review.
Swift also said that Railtrack had a long way to go before he could be satisfied that the long-term health of the network was assured.

Railtrack has countered criticism of its performance by pledging to press ahead with plans to spend 15.9 billion pounds over the next 10 years on maintaining, renovating and developing its network. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
